summary: Frontend-only test of the generic Legacy->Advanced permission bridge. I tested 4 logins (admin, Saeed, Salim, layer2_test_emp) by checking which SideMenu items show and by opening /students, /manage-teachers, /faculty-board and /alumni. I also smoke-tested /offline-sync-report and the full-screen role modal in /advanced-access-control. RESULT: the bridge FAILS its core goal of being precisely scoped. layer2_test_emp has only 3 keys (students_ser_create_student, students_ser_delete_student, grades_grades_download_grades_template), but his menu shows items he has no keys for: Courses (المقررات), Teachers (إدارة المعلمين), Alumni (الخريجون), Attendance (إدارة الحضور) and Enrollments (إدارة التسجيلات). Faculty Board (مجلس الكلية) is correctly hidden. Salim and Saeed: the filter code they use did not change, and their menus/pages load real data (Saeed 72 students, 4 teachers; Salim 19 students, 13 teachers). There was no saved pre-change menu to compare against, so 'exactly the same as before' is shown by code review, not by a before/after run. Admin has one regression: 'محاضراتي' (teacherOnly item) now shows for admin. Smoke tests passed.

ui_bugs.issue: Real-enforcement user layer2_test_emp (students_* + grades_* keys only) sees 'المقررات', 'إدارة المعلمين', 'الخريجون', 'إدارة الحضور', 'إدارة التسجيلات'. ROOT CAUSE: LEGACY_TO_ADV_GROUPS is built from legacy_permissions_detected, which only records that a legacy permission string appears somewhere in a group's code. That is co-occurrence, not equivalence. For example manage_courses->[...,'students',...], manage_teachers->[...,'students',...], manage_students->['alumni',...,'students',...], view_attendance->['reports','students','attendance'], manage_enrollments->[...,'students'], import_data->[...,'students']. So any students_* key turns on all of these legacy permissions. SideMenu step 3 (hasAnyPermission(item.permissions)) also runs even when the item has its own precise advPermissionKeys, so the precise check is overridden.

Admin regression: 'محاضراتي' (my-lectures, teacherOnly) now shows for admin. `if (isAdmin) return true` was moved ABOVE the teacherOnly check. Before this change the teacherOnly check ran first and hid the item for admin.

For layer2_test_emp the 'الخريجون' menu item shows (via the bridge), but clicking /alumni redirects to /no-permission. The menu and the route guard disagree. The item should not show at all with his current keys.

The page loads (no redirect), but GET /api/students returns 403 and the page shows 'غير مصرح لك بعرض الطلاب' with 0 students. This is correct backend behavior: the user has create/delete keys but NO list key (students_ser_get_students). The review's expectation that he sees his department's students cannot be met with the current 3 keys. The page still shows Add/Import/Export buttons even though he cannot list students.

integration_issues.issue: AuthContext.hasPermission/hasAnyPermission/hasAllPermissions now use the same over-broad group map in EVERY page. Page buttons and sections (not just the menu) will leak for real-enforcement users, e.g. manage-teachers loads its UI and then GET /api/teachers returns 403.

action_items: Redesign LEGACY_TO_ADV_GROUPS as an EQUIVALENCE map (each legacy permission -> its own primary group or specific keys only). Examples: manage_students/view_students/add_student/... -> ['students'], manage_courses/view_courses -> ['courses'], manage_teachers/view_teachers -> ['teachers'], manage_enrollments/view_enrollments -> ['enrollments'], view_attendance/manage_attendance -> ['attendance']. Do NOT derive it from legacy_permissions_detected co-occurrence. Alumni should map only from an alumni_* key, not from manage_students.
Better still, map legacy permissions to action-level keys (read vs create vs delete), so 'view_*' needs a list/get key, not any key in the group.
In SideMenu, for real-enforced users: if an item defines advPermissionKeys or advGroups, use ONLY that precise check and skip the hasAnyPermission bridge fallback.
Restore the teacherOnly check before `if (isAdmin) return true` (or exclude teacherOnly items for admin) so 'محاضراتي' is hidden for admin again.
After fixing, re-run: layer2_test_emp menu should show only 'إدارة الطلاب' among the academic items (plus forAll items such as الإعدادات الأساسية/المهام/الخطابات الرسمية, if intended).
critical_code_review_comments: legacyPermissionBridge.ts: the map is co-occurrence data, not equivalence data. Its own comment says it is 'not manual guessing', but the scan only shows where a permission string appears, not what it means. This makes the bridge over-permissive by design.
SideMenu.tsx line ~242: moving `if (isAdmin) return true` above teacherOnly changes behavior for admin. The roles/adminOnly checks were also moved, but those are harmless for legacy users.
faculty-board.tsx canManage now accepts any councils_* key, so even a read-only councils key unlocks manage UI. Server-side enforcement still protects actions, but the UI over-exposes them.

AuthContext: AuthContext gets the user from its own state, while SideMenu reads useAuthStore. The authStore reset() on logout clears the realEnforcementStore, which is good, but there are two sources of user truth.

success_rate.frontend: 55% - legacy users: Saeed/Salim OK, admin has 1 regression (my-lectures); real-enforcement bridge has 5 leaking menu items; smoke tests OK

seed_data_creation: None. No data was created or modified.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Login form: inputs with placeholder 'اسم المستخدم / رقم القيد / الرقم المرجعي' and 'كلمة المرور', button text 'تسجيل الدخول'. Menu: [data-testid=floating-menu-btn]. Check effective keys with GET /api/advanced-access/me/effective-access. layer2_test_emp currently has 3 keys. Expected after the fix: Courses/Teachers/Alumni/Attendance/Enrollments hidden for him, and admin does not see 'محاضراتي'.
rca of the issue: Reproduce: log in as layer2_test_emp/test1234 and open the side menu; Courses, Teachers, Alumni, Attendance and Enrollments show. Why: SideMenu step 3 calls hasAnyPermission(['manage_courses',...]); in AuthContext, hasAdvancedAccessForLegacy('manage_courses', keys) checks groups ['academic_structure','courses','curriculum','general_tools','schedule','students','system_tools']; the key 'students_ser_create_student' starts with 'students_', so it returns true. Fix: use an equivalence map, and use only the precise advPermissionKeys/advGroups check when the item defines them.
